### [Bluetooth brakes are broken as researchers find anyone can control them](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/23/bluetooth-brakes-are-broken-as-researchers-find-anyone-can-control-them/5311748)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 19:29 UTC · en

> Security fixes are available for two Elecbrakes models, but an older controller remains vulnerable and unpatched

> 來源提供的正文:
> Imagine something as mission-critical as the brakes on a trailer being vulnerable to unauthorized control. One Australian manufacturer made the interesting choice of building Bluetooth into a trailer brake controller without adequately securing its critical braking functions. Anyone within Bluetooth range of an unpatched Elecbrakes trailer controller could potentially trigger its brakes or apply more braking force than intended, without needing to authenticate. The discovery comes courtesy of a pair of security researchers from Element Digital, Patrick Forck and Jeremy McCarthy. Their investigation began earlier this year when Forck was driving down the road and noticed that his physical Elecbrakes In-Car Remote had connected to someone else's trailer without pairing or prompting him. “It had connected mid-drive, without pairing or a prompt, to a brake controller that wasn’t mine, on a trailer I’d never seen, belonging to a driver who had no idea,” the researchers wrote. That one-off connection triggered a full-scale investigation by the pair. For those unfamiliar with trailer brake controllers, these devices are commonly used on larger trailers. Australian manufacturer Elecbrakes sells such controllers in Australia and New Zealand. Depending on jurisdiction, trailers over a certain weight are required to have their own braking system, which Elecbrakes manufactures. Elecbrakes offers two versions that are designed to be easier to install than traditional controllers: One that’s mounted in a vehicle, and one that is mounted directly on a trailer. That trailer-mounted unit can receive Bluetooth commands from the Elecbrakes smartphone app or a separate in-car remote. Given the importance of such control units to road safety, it’s easy to imagine how serious such a vulnerability could be if it proved to be easy to exploit, and boy, did it. Forck and McCarthy admitted they’re infrastructure security guys, not software devs, so they turned to Claude Code to dissect a decompiled copy of the Elecbrakes app, which Claude was happy to oblige. “What came back from the analysis was a map of the device’s entire Bluetooth GATT profile: 47 characteristics across four services, commands sent as plain unencrypted byte arrays, no checksums, no sequence numbers,” the researchers noted. To make matters worse, there was no authentication required for critical braking commands, even though other Bluetooth functions required pairing. Claude then built a web app that ran in Chrome which was able to access the Bluetooth controls for a nearby Elecbrakes system, and they were able to modify practically every aspect of brake control on a unit owned by one of them. Pairing failed on a few attempts, but not where it mattered: It allowed the connection without issue for actual brake control. They sent a few bytes to the brake control characteristic, and were shocked. “The electromagnetic hum at the brake drums was immediate and, frankly, a little sickening,” the pair said. “It said yes to four bytes from a total stranger then energised several tonnes’ worth of brakes and reported back that it had done so, pleased with itself.” Further experiments managed to modify braking strength based on deceleration speed as well, making it so that the trailer acted unpredictably based on the amount of force a driver applied to stop their vehicle. To say this is worse than a typical internet-connected device bug is to put it mildly - it even earned a trio of CVEs from CISA, with two of them scoring a CVSS of 9.6. “The attack surface is ‘anyone within Bluetooth range,’ the skill required is ‘can write four bytes,’ and the victim selection is ‘optional,’ ” Forck and McCarthy said. The fact AI was able to get them to that point in just a couple of days is even more concerning, they added. “This kind of research used to require a fairly rare and specific skill set,” the pair noted. “It now requires curiosity, a device you own, and an AI that can read bytecode faster than any human.” Luckily, they appear to have been dealing with a relatively responsive company in Elecbrakes - patches have been deployed for both the in-car and trailer-mounted models of their brake controllers. Installation is a manual process, we note, so if you own a controller from the company, be sure to stop and install the update. Unfortunately, Elecbrakes has a third controller out there that hasn’t been manufactured in several years, and it got skipped in the patching process. Owners of an ELBC2000 should be aware that their controller is still vulnerable, and there’s no patch available yet, as the vendor didn’t confirm that the ELBC2000 was vulnerable until the end of October, after it faced pressure from the researchers. ®

### [Critical Cisco remote code execution bug under attack](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/23/critical-cisco-remote-code-execution-bug-under-attack/5311722)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 17:56 UTC · en

> CISA, F6 sound the alarm after PoC exploit made public

> 來源提供的正文:
> Attackers are currently exploiting a critical vulnerability tracked as CVE-2026-76466 in Cisco Expressway that allows them to remotely execute commands as root without any authentication, according to warnings from the US government and security researchers. CVE-2026-76466, which carries a 9.8 CVSS rating, affects Cisco Expressway-C and Cisco Expressway-E gateways configured in clusters, both virtual and physical appliances running vulnerable software. These provide firewall traversal, VPN-less remote access, and call routing for remote users connecting to voice, video, and messaging collaboration services. The bug involves hard-coded authentication credentials and insufficient certificate validation in clustered Expressway deployments. “An attacker with possession of the cookies could exploit this vulnerability by connecting to the database service and invoking specific remote procedure call (RPC) commands,” Cisco said in October, when it disclosed the bug and issued a software update that fixed the flaw. “A successful exploit could allow the attacker to execute arbitrary commands as root on the underlying operating system of an affected device.” At the time, the networking vendor said it wasn’t aware of any abuse of the vulnerability. That all changed late last week, however, when Russian security firm F6 said it was investigating “the first observed case” of miscreants exploiting CVE-2026-76466, shortly after a public proof-of-concept exploit became available. “The attackers initially compromised two Cisco Expressway internet-facing devices,” F6’s Cyber Defense Center said on Thursday. “Through one of them, they gained access to two additional cluster nodes located on the organization’s internal network. After obtaining root access, the attackers began preparing tooling for further lateral movement across the infrastructure.” Specifically, the criminals prepared custom Python code to scan the victim’s network and identify files and folders shared over the Server Message Block (SMB) protocol. The scripts were also designed to interact with SQL Server and WinRM, and search GitLab repositories for credentials and other sensitive information. The Python scripts used in the attack indicated that the operator used an AI assistant, according to F6. The security shop also noted that one of the key indicators of compromise is a nodeup “wombat@127.0.0.1” entry in the Erlang system log (erlang.log) on affected Cisco Expressway devices. A day later, the US Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency (CISA) added CVE-2026-76466 to its Known Exploited Vulnerabilities catalog, and told federal agencies to patch by Monday. Cisco updated its advisory on Monday to acknowledge CISA’s addition, while noting that it has no direct evidence of active exploitation. The Register reached out to the networking and security vendor for additional details about the scope of the attacks, but did not receive any response. We will update this story as we learn more. ®

### [Bulgaria evicts cyber snoops who lurked inside government networks for 5 years](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/23/bulgaria-evicts-cyber-snoops-who-lurked-inside-government-networks-for-5-years/5311629)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 17:01 UTC · en

> Minister says intruders downloaded more than 130 GB of data as political churn left security neglected

> 來源提供的正文:
> The Ancient Thracian heartland of Bulgaria says it has shut down a cyberespionage operation that gave intruders access to government networks for five years – the longest-running known campaign against its administration. Bulgaria's Ministry of Innovation and Digital Transformation said the unauthorized and officially unattributed attackers first gained access to infrastructure used by government institutions to exchange information in 2021. It explained that the intrusion went unnoticed for so long because "the previous means of protection did not work as a single, integrated system," and that without a new, recently installed product, it may have gone undetected for much longer. "The incident was discovered thanks to the new national cybersecurity system, which for the first time provides a single picture of what is happening in state networks," the ministry added. "Without it, this activity would most likely have remained hidden for an indefinite period of time." Bulgaria acknowledged that "sensitive information related to the work of the state" was accessed, but did not specify the scale of the compromise. Innovation and Digital Transformation Minister Ivan Vasilev said attackers had downloaded more than 130 GB of data over five years. He also put the volume at 62 million pages. The Register contacted the Bulgarian government for confirmation of these numbers. The ministry said that it has not yet found any evidence that citizens' personal data was compromised, and that the affected infrastructure "will be under increased surveillance for 90 days" in case the attackers try to regain access. Vasilev said multiple international hacking groups had accessed government systems since 2021. He did not specify the names of these groups, however, nor did he name any specific countries that may have been involved. In a follow-up interview with bTV, Vasilev blamed political instability and frequent changes of ministerial leadership for leaving government systems inadequately protected. A representative of the Progressive Bulgaria party, which back in May won Bulgaria's eighth general election in five years, Vasilev said the "constant change of leadership" means "important things for the state do not actually happen." Vasilev said the intrusion was discovered over the summer as the national cybersecurity system was upgraded, and that teams had spent the past three to four months removing the attackers. ®

> Rogue AI or nation-state hackers would be preferable to the amount of technical debt the past week of wobbling services laid bare

> 來源提供的正文:
> Have you or someone you love been affected by a tech outage this week? Yeah, us too. You can listen to the latest episode of The Kettle right here on this page, as well as on Spotify, Apple Music, or YouTube. Those platforms also let you subscribe to The Kettle, so you are always notified when the latest episode goes live In a week of big stories the biggest one seems to be the fact that everyone from Microsoft to the NSA was dealing with outages, and here's what might be the worst part: It doesn't seem to be AI, nor hostile countries intent on destroying our infrastructure. Unfortunately for all of us, what the past week of outages reveal is that – as we discussed on The Kettle less than a month ago – all of our essential tech infrastructure is basically held together with duct tape and twine. Join host Brandon Vigliarolo, cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons, and open source reporter Liam Proven to discuss what comes next, and whether we can fix any of this without tearing all of it out and starting from scratch. A lightly edited transcript is included below: Brandon (00:04) Hi everyone and welcome to the latest episode of the Register's Kettle podcast. I'm your host, Reg reporter Brandon Vigliarolo, and if you're hearing this, then that means there isn't an outage right now, which seems like that might be a lot to ask of our technology in the past week. It's been a busy week. We had Anthropic's IPO, Nvidia drama continuing, and other stuff going on. But the one thing that everyone seems to be talking about is what's become known in the zeitgeist as Outagepalooza, as it seems like everything was offline at some point in the past few days. With me to discuss the chaos and the conspiracy theories they're giving rise to is Reg cybersecurity editor Jessica Lyons and our open source reporter Liam Proven. Guys, what's happening? Jessica Lyons (00:45) I've got my tinfoil hat on right now, so I'm ready. Brandon (00:48) Yes, I've had family calling me being like, my god, what's happening? Who's ending the world right now? Is it AI? Jessica Lyons (00:55) Ha ha ha. Brandon (00:56) We'll get to that part. Liam Proven (00:57) Wonderful. My mum's wardrobe door stuck this week and we found a company on the little rock in the middle of the Irish Sea that fixes sliding doors and he didn't get my emails because he's one hundred percent Microsoft and he uses Hotmail and it's Hotmail. Liam Proven (01:18) And when I got it through, you'd be amazed at the ramifications. I SMS'd him in the end and he got that and then was really angry because I said, "Dude, I've been trying to get you for three days. Can you at least reply and say Friday?" ### [Norway links energy firm cyberattacks to critical Azure API Management flaw](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/23/norway-links-energy-firm-cyberattacks-to-critical-azure-api-management-flaw/5311598)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 12:29 UTC · en

> Microsoft says mitigation is in place, but admins must investigate possible compromise and rotate secrets

> 來源提供的正文:
> Microsoft has issued a critical vulnerability advisory after attackers were caught raiding Azure API Management (APIM) instances for secrets and performing admin operations. According to a nonpublic advisory, seen by The Register, Microsoft said the attacks, which have already affected two major energy companies, only impact customers on Azure API Management Classic tiers, not Azure API Management v2. It said of the now-patched vuln: "Our investigation found that customers were exposed and an unauthorized party could have used the issue to access secrets stored in Azure API Management Classic instances before Microsoft identified the security issue." Microsoft linked exposure to Classic-tier configurations that did not follow its network security guidance or stored secrets directly in APIM rather than referencing them from Azure Key Vault. Microsoft directs customers to its security guidance for the recommended configuration. The advisory lists potentially exposed secrets, including named values, client secrets associated with identity providers and OpenID Connect providers, subscription keys, and tokens used to call direct management APIs. Security expert Anders Kristiansen warned that stolen credentials could also give attackers access to services behind APIM. "If someone obtains a credential from that configuration, they may be able to use it directly against the service it protects, outside APIM," he wrote. "What they can reach depends on the credential's permissions and whether it is still valid." Norway's National Security Authority (NSM) urged organizations using APIM to assume their secrets and named values had been exposed and rotate all tokens and secrets. The agency also advised mapping the information accessible through each APIM instance to assess the potential scope of any compromise. NSM credited Norway's energy sector with first detecting the vulnerability last week. It named gas giant Equinor and hydropower company Skagerak Energi among the affected organizations. The authority commended Equinor for its early detection and rapid information-sharing, and warned that growing use of AI increased the risk of further exploitation. "The vulnerability affects several sectors in Norway and also beyond Norway's borders," it said. "NSM has close dialogue and cooperation with national and international partners and businesses about the situation. "When a vulnerability becomes known, multiple actors will be able to attempt to exploit it. Rapid escalation in the use of artificial intelligence is affecting the situation. This poses a risk to Norwegian businesses." Customers who spoke to The Register warned that forgotten development and test instances could leave more organizations exposed. The extent of exploitation remains unclear. Microsoft said it identified the security issue on November 18 and automatically applied a mitigation to close the access path the following day. The Windows giant said customers still needed to investigate whether their instances had been compromised before the mitigation was applied. NSM nevertheless advised organizations to check their instance's runtime version against its published patch thresholds and contact their provider if it remained unpatched. Microsoft did not immediately respond to our request for comment. ®

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 11:48 UTC · en

> Payments platform hasn't disclosed how the data was captured or the scale of the breach

> 來源提供的正文:
> Software e-commerce platform Cleverbridge has admitted that hackers stole customers' card numbers and CVV security codes, raising questions about how the attackers captured data that payment security rules prohibit retaining after authorization. The Germany-headquartered company, which handles software sales and subscriptions on behalf of other businesses, detected unauthorized activity on its platform on November 4. In an incident update, Cleverbridge said it had cut off the intruders' access and launched an investigation that later established payment card information had been copied from its systems. The public notice doesn't spell out exactly what was stolen, but an email sent to affected customers, seen by The Register, fills in some rather important blanks. "Based on our investigation to date, the information involved includes payment card details you used to make a purchase through Cleverbridge, notably your card number, expiry date, card security code (CVV/CVC), and contact details," the company told customers. Email addresses, billing addresses, and phone numbers were also among the information potentially exposed, although Cleverbridge reckons account passwords escaped the breach. More concerning are the stolen CVV codes. PCI DSS rules prohibit retaining card verification codes after authorization, even in encrypted form. Cleverbridge hasn't explained how the attackers obtained the codes, whether they were retained after transactions, or whether the criminals intercepted them during payment processing. The company didn't respond to The Register's questions about the breach. Cleverbridge handles the business of selling software online, from taking payments to managing subscriptions, and its client roster includes some familiar names in enterprise IT, such as Red Hat, SUSE, Tenable, Veeam, Jamf, Parallels, and Plesk. That doesn't mean customers of all those companies had their card details stolen. Cleverbridge hasn't named the vendors affected by the intrusion, nor has it disclosed how many people were caught up in the breach or how long the hackers were poking around its systems. In its notification to customers, the company said it had contacted data protection authorities, payment card schemes, and its payment partners, and was working with a specialist police cybercrime unit. It began notifying affected individuals on November 20, more than two weeks after discovering the intrusion. Affected customers are being offered 24 months of free credit monitoring and fraud assistance. That may help detect identity misuse, but it won't stop a crook armed with their card number, expiration date, and CVV from attempting a fraudulent purchase. Two years of credit monitoring is a nice gesture, but customers whose card numbers and CVVs are now in criminal hands might prefer a new bit of plastic. ®

### [When Microsoft, Apple, and the FAA can't keep it up, it's a system of a down](https://www.theregister.com/columnists/2026/11/23/when-microsoft-apple-and-the-faa-cant-keep-it-up-its-a-system-of-a-down/5311363)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 08:42 UTC · en

> Outage after outage after outage is a syndrome that needs radical treatment

> 來源提供的正文:
> No Access November is going well this year. Among the many organizations to adopt Outage As A Service (OAAS) were Microsoft, Apple, the FAA, and any number of European supermarkets. Even the NSA has succumbed. For us, at least, outage is word of the year. It's certainly deeply embedded in the public mind, with schoolchildren reportedly referring to the 19th century Irish famine as "the potato outage." There's no danger of an outrage outage. OAAS is synonymous with infrastructure failure, a more useful term that begins to hint at cause and cure as well as effect. In all of the latest crop, what we know is depressingly familiar. Microsoft's O365 meltdown was a cascading failure caused by a botched upgrade that took stuff offline and melted down as it tried to come back. The FAA was a migration from Jurassic hardware that wasn't end of life so much as living fossil. The Eurofridge-cum-fondue-maker was a control system so badly written it fell apart if you raised an eyebrow at it. Clearly, nobody had. Until now. These are all different classes of OAAS that have been around for decades. Security-based outages are still outages, and a packet flood is still a packet flood whether it's a botnet DDoS or finger trouble in the config dashboard. Each of them has a root cause with obvious fixes – a faulty mental model of network/server interaction, chronic underfunding, a complete supply chain with little cyber-security expertise. All these, like the poor, will be with us always. They won't fix themselves. Infrastructure that works is invisible, and invisible things are forgotten until they break. What's needed is an infrastructure that watches itself, that is designed to be adaptive and resilient, one that refuses to connect to danger and nulls out any that gets through. There have been attempts to create a ground-up architecture that is inherently risk resistant. One such is SCION (Scalability, Control, and Isolation On Next-generation networks). It redesigns routing between domains around explicit path selection, separate control and data planes, and mechanisms for trust and failure isolation. The result is a very resilient, very reliable, and very secure infrastructure that reflects the designers' tenet that you can't patch the internet into any of these things. Start from scratch or GTFO. SCION started about 15 years ago, and it works well enough to be adopted by entities like the Secure Swiss Finance Network. If the Gnomes of Zurich trust it, no higher accreditation exists. Well, it was designed by ETH Zürich. Where you won't find it is almost everywhere else. The internet is like Switzerland in the same way the Amazon rainforest is like Central Park. There are trees and sometimes it rains. It is unwise to infer anything else. Given you can't manicure existing infrastructure into true resilience, the only other option is evolution. A couple of billion years of continued life on Earth has proved this is the only way to re-engineer complex systems while they're usefully running. In this case, the current evolutionary endpoint that's of most interest is the human immune system. An interlocking system of functions, it takes care of uncountably thousands of pathogen-based threats and internal malfunctions every day. You might think that the 30-odd billion computing machines making up today's Internet are impossible to monitor and secure, but that's peanuts to the human immune system. An average human has around 30 trillion cells, and roughly the same again in bacteria. When it works, the mechanics of the human infrastructure are invisible and out of mind. The immune system makes it so, and everything involved is driven by information, signaling and behavior. There is pattern matching, resource management, defense in depth and reinforcement learning in persistent models. Sounds familiar? The analogy between this and modern digital infrastructure is so irresistible that it has been around for a lifetime. Viruses, infections, swarms, worms, system health are so familiar that they go unremarked. The term Digital Immune System has been around since the last century too, pushed by outfits like IBM, Symantec and Gartner. It hasn't taken off, probably because it's been marketing bunkum instead of describing the development of inherently resilient infrastructure based on insights from biology. It has also been true that natural selection, the engine of evolution and this biology, only works in IT at the most macro, capitalist level of product and company survival. Everything else is selected through design decisions, market analysis, and insight versus delusion. The adoption of immunological concepts to digital infrastructure will have to be the result of rigorous exploration of complex systems and cross-disciplinary research. What would that look like? There are academics thinking just these thoughts: see this paper [PDF] from Kay Smarsly at Technische Universität Hamburg. Like SCION, it takes an architectural look at what resiliency might look like, but with explicit reference to biological systems. OAAS is a chronic syndrome with multiple causes and potentially fatal outcomes. It exists and persists because digital infrastructure too often fails to contain internal failures or external attacks. We have a working example of an approach to managing analogous problems in systems far vaster and more intricate than any we have built. We now have tools that may start to do systemic analysis and inference at a useful scale. In an industry prepared to bet billions on agents that do your shopping, there is every reason to kick off serious research into digital immune systems worthy of the name. Doctor, cure thyself. ®

### [Google claims last week’s critical VMware bug was under attack in September](https://www.theregister.com/virtualization/2026/11/23/google-claims-last-weeks-critical-vmware-bug-was-under-attack-in-september/5311547)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 04:39 UTC · en

> China-linked ARMORY CASTLE knew about it weeks before it unleashed five custom malware tools targeting vCenter

> 來源提供的正文:
> Google’s Mandiant unit has claimed that the critical flaw VMware last week revealed in its vCenter product was under attack by a China-linked threat actor which knew of the bug in July and exploited it in September. VMware revealed several flaws on November 19. The big nasty is CVE-2026-123890, which allows unauthorized access to vCenter, the management console for hosts and guest VMs. According to seven researchers from Google’s threat intelligence group (formerly Mandiant), a crew it calls ARMORY CASTLE that it suspects of having links to the People’s Republic of China exploited CVE-2026-123890 by first compromising remote access appliances from BeyondTrust. Google’s analysis suggests the crew uses that toehold to establish access to other Linux appliances before moving deeper into victims’ networks. If the crew finds vCenter, it deploys a custom malware tool called “BONESAW” designed to slice into the VMware product. In the incident Google observed, BONESAW let attackers “forge authentication tokens, bypass MFA, and impersonate any user.” The gang put that access to work by conducting an inventory of the victim’s VMware setup, scooping up data describing the ESXi file system, attached disks, and mounted Virtual Machine File System volumes. ARMORY CASTLE also added an SSH public key to the root account’s authorized keys, and “conducted further reconnaissance and data theft on the ESXi filesystem using the root account.” Google also found evidence of BONESAW being used in July, on a server an unidentified entity had patched against CVE-2026-59309 – another authentication bypass vulnerability in vCenter. And BONESAW was just one of five tools Google thinks ARMORY CASTLE created as part of its plan to attack vCenter. It also made webshells named SLIMSAVAGE and CAGEMATCH, a backdoor called BEARBONES, and a SAML utility called SAWSNAKE. “The use of three separate specialized sets of malware and two zero-days in the course of a single campaign indicates that there are significant resources supporting ARMORY CASTLE operations,” Google’s researchers wrote. “It also shows the extent of the threat actor’s operational commitment to compromise high priority targets.” Few targets are as juicy as vCenter, because it can literally give attackers access to thousands of virtual machines and the hosts they run on. Google hasn't said how many attacks is saw on vCenter using BONESAW. The Register asked VMware if it was aware of the September attack, if it took any measures to defend its customers at the time, and to share a timeline for disclosure and remediation of CVE-2026-123890. A spokesperson responded by pointing to VMware’s Q&A document and stating “In today's threat environment, customers should assume any publicly disclosed critical vulnerability can and will be exploited by threat actors under the right conditions and should apply the recommended patches immediately.” VMware has tried to make that easier by adding non-disruptive patching to several of its products, and introducing a product called vDefend that offers “virtual patching” by creating compensating controls that use network micro segmentation and other techniques to block access to resources malware uses. Last month, VMware debuted another new tool, HyperArmor, to block incoming malicious traffic targeting its VCF private cloud suite. In recent discussions with The Register, VMware execs told us the Broadcom business unit will emphasize security improvements in future product releases. “Our teams have integrated frontier AI security model testing directly into our engineering workflows, strengthened our software supply chain to reduce third-party dependencies and speed up upstream responses, and built VCF 9.1 specifically for high-velocity security,” a spokesperson said in response to questions about the Mandiant report. Freebie patches hard to find One security offering VMware won’t continue is free access to patches for zero-day flaws in supported versions of products sold under its old perpetual licenses – even to users who don’t have an ongoing support deal or software subscription. VMware last year stopped making those patches available for download and promised it would establish “a separate patch delivery cycle.” Readers have pointed out that information about the new cycle isn’t easy to find, and The Register noticed that the blog post in which Broadcom CEO Hock Tan promised the free patches no longer contains references to the offer. Removing the promise seems to be a recent edit as an Internet Archive snapshot of the page from October 20 does mention the zero-day patch freebies. A VMware spokesperson told us the free zero-day patch policy remains in place despite changes to the post. “Broadcom’s policy to provide access to zero-day critical security patches to customers who, at their own risk, continue to run perpetual VMware vSphere 8 software without an active support agreement, remains in place,” the spokesperson wrote. “Those customers can get these patches by contacting Broadcom. This policy covers vSphere 8 patches only and is expected to remain in effect through the end of general support on October 11, 2027.” ®

### [$1 of GPT-5.1 tokens finds new ways around China’s Great Firewall](https://www.theregister.com/security/2026/11/23/1-of-gpt-51-tokens-finds-new-ways-around-chinas-great-firewall/5311532)

`rss:theregister_security` · T2 · 2026-11-23 00:23 UTC · en

> PLUS: Lenovo's infra group finally makes big profit; Indonesia’s glaciers are gone; Australian bank releases its AI bug-finder; and more!

> 來源提供的正文:
> Researchers have found new ways to evade China’s Great Firewall after spending just $1 worth of tokens. That result appeared last week in a paper titled “CircumVolve: Automated Discovery of Censorship Evasion Strategies Using Large Language Models” presented at the Conference on Computer and Communications Security run by the Association for Computing Machinery’s Special Interest Group on Security, Audit and Control. Penned by six researchers from the University of Massachusetts Amherst, University of Colorado Boulder, and activist group the Great Firewall Report, the paper points out that finding holes in the Great Firewall is a laborious process – so just the kind of task worth handing to AI. The authors came up with a tool they call “CircumVolve” and describe as “a system for automated discovery of censorship circumvention strategies across the full network stack.” “CircumVolve combines LLM code generation with iterative feedback-driven evaluation to produce verifiable and deployable evasion techniques,” they wrote. “CircumVolve models different censorship techniques as discrete scenarios, each capturing the specific context, protocol constraints, and blocking mechanisms of real-world censors. Within each scenario, evasion strategies are represented as executable Python programs that implement packet and protocol manipulations — from rewriting TCP/IP header fields, to crafting DNS queries that exploit parser ambiguities, to modifying the internal structure of encrypted QUIC Initial packets — while maintaining protocol correctness within tolerable bounds or strategically violating it when beneficial.” The authors tested CircumVolve on simulated censorship tools used by China, Iran, Pakistan, and Kazakhstan, and on virtual private servers deployed on clouds in those countries. Those tests found the median API cost to the first successful evasion was less than $1 in token expenditure costs when using GPT-5.1. The authors acknowledge that operators of censorship infrastructure might be able to observe CircumVolve at work, but feel its relatively small payloads – 80 KB of outgoing and 150 KB of incoming traffic – and 25-45-second pauses between tests might see it fly under the radar. “CircumVolve represents a first step in leveraging LLMs to accelerate the censorship-circumvention lifecycle,” the authors wrote. “By automating the labor-intensive tasks of protocol analysis, implementation, and testing, AI-driven approaches make studying circumvention capabilities far more accessible to the comparatively under-resourced Internet freedom community [and] demonstrates how AI-assisted systems can narrow the resource gap between Internet freedom advocates and well-funded censoring states.” Lenovo finally cracks monster datacenter profits Ever since acquiring IBM’s x86 server business in 2014, Chinese hardware giant Lenovo has struggled to turn a profit from datacenter sales, even as it expanded its business into storage, networking, and selling to hyperscalers. The AI boom has finally done what various strategy shifts and waves of hype could not: propel the company’s Infrastructure Solutions Group (ISG) to a $1 billion quarterly profit. In its Q2 results announcement [PDF] last week, the company revealed ISG revenue hit a quarterly record of $11.3 billion, up 178 percent year-over-year, and that lovely big profit. At a time when enterprise hardware supply chains are tight, Lenovo says it was able to increase shipments of x86 servers and even emerge as the largest vendor of such systems with 16 percent market share. Lenovo also claimed it’s moved further ahead as the planet’s premier PC provider, by pointing to 15 percent year-on-year growth for its intelligent devices group where quarterly revenue reached $17.4 billion. The company claims it has 23.8 percent of the PC market and now has seven percent more market share than its closest rival, Apple. The company said premium devices account for 63 percent of its PC business Overall revenue rose 48 percent year over year to $30.24 billion for the quarter. Indonesia’s glaciers are all but gone It may surprise readers to know that Indonesia, the nation that spreads across 17,000 islands in the tropical latitudes of 11°S to 6°N, is home to alpine regions sufficiently high that glaciers can form. Indonesia’s glaciers clung to the top of Puncak Jaya, aka Carstenz Pyramid, a 4,884-meter peak on New Guinea at 4°S. Sadly, an assessment published last week by NASA says the glaciers have probably melted to the point at which not much is left other than a few patches of ice. NASA last week posted images that show glaciers covering 4.31 km2 atop Puncak Jaya in 1988, and another from this year that shows most of that ice is gone. Images from September 2025 apparently showed just .09km2 of ice remained. “To qualify as a glacier, a body of ice generally has to be thick enough to flow downhill under its own weight, and it needs an area where snow builds up faster than it melts,” NASA’s Kathryn Hansen wrote. “Puncak Jaya’s remaining ice has thinned so much and broken into such small, stagnant patches that it no longer flows.” For what it’s worth, commercial operators run expeditions to Puncak Jaya. Peak-baggers seek it out because some consider it the highest mountain in Australasia/Oceania and therefore one of the “Seven Summits” – the highest point on each continent. The Reg won’t get into the debate about the validity of including Puncak Jaya on that list, but if you fancy some equatorial alpine action your correspondent recently climbed Malaysia’s 4,095m Mount Kinabalu. It’s an overnight walk that requires no technical skills or gear, but definitely demands supple knees. The peak was clearly glaciated in the distant past but snow is now extremely rare on Kinabalu. Australian bank giving away its bug-hunter Here’s an odd one: Australia’s Commonwealth Bank (CBA) created an AI-powered tool to scan its bespoke code for bugs, and has now packaged it as a free release called “CodeCheck.” The bank says analyzes the output of OpenAI’s Codex and Anthropic’s Claude Code with “a consistent process for analyzing code, investigating potential vulnerabilities and providing information to assist engineers.” Apparently, it is “ based on an approach used within CBA, but it is not the same as, and does not represent, the systems, tools or controls CBA uses internally.” The bank posted CodeCheck to GitHub, where it warns the project is “a one-time open-source release for businesses to evaluate” and that it will not actively maintain, update, or support the code. Japan’s space program hands some launches to Mitsubishi Japan’s Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) last week announced it has reached an agreement with Mitsubishi Heavy Industries (MHI) to take over responsibility for running launches of its flagship H3 rocket when used in certain configurations. The deal means MHI will handle launches for H3s that use a pair of LE-9 liquid-fuel engines alongside two SRB-3 solid-fuel boosters. JAXA will continue running launches that use different, or experimental, configurations. Once JAXA is satisfied those new rigs are reliable, it plans to transition them to private operators, too. ®

> - **边看边听无缝切换**：书页里点哪句就从哪句开始念，自动跟读翻页，停下接着看还在原位置；自带免配置自然人声和 125MB 离线语音包，也可接自己的语音接口。
> - **小说广播剧模式**：支持多角色广播剧朗读，自动或手动给书里不同人物分配不同声音、搭配环境音（接上大模型可辅助识别台词角色）。
> - **听播客与有声书**：支持 RSS 订阅播客、导入有声书，听的时候也能对照内容随手划线记笔记。
> - **外文查词与防剧透问答**：内置离线词典，点词查释义、双击翻整句；可连本机 Ollama 或 DeepSeek 问书中内容，默认只读已看章节不剧透。
> - **笔记导出与网盘同步**：划线和想法随时导出 Markdown、带划线 EPUB，或发往 Obsidian / Notion / flomo / Anki；多端用自己的 iCloud 或 WebDAV 同步（Google Drive 即将支持）。
>
> **适合谁用：**
> 平时自己管理本地电子书 / NAS 书库、喜欢边看边听或听小说广播剧、读英文原著，以及习惯用 Obsidian 记笔记的朋友。
>
> **技术实现：**
> - **跨端核心**：**Rust + SQLite**（电子书解析、中英断句、全文检索与同步合并）
> - **各端界面**：macOS / iOS 端用 **SwiftUI**，Android 端用 **Kotlin + Jetpack Compose**，开发中的 Windows 端为 **WinUI 3 / C#**
> - **排版与语音**：书页排字分页用 **TypeScript** 跑在系统自带 WebView 中，离线朗读基于本地 ONNX 语音模型，包体积小、启动也比较轻快
>
> **目前状态与未完善项：**
> 刚发 0.1.0 第一版，**Mac（Apple Silicon）** 和 **Android** 可在 Releases 直接下载 `.dmg` / `.apk` 使用（Mac 未签付费证书，首次打开需在系统「隐私与安全性」点一次“仍要打开”）。**Windows 版**正在开发中，**iOS 版**暂未上商店需自签 `.ipa`；**广播剧角色识别与配音效果、有声书自动对齐、书房电台**也还在继续打磨。
>
> GitHub 仓库：https://github.com/inokoru/yuyue
> 安装包下载：https://github.com/inokoru/yuyue/releases
>
> 刚发第一版肯定还有粗糙的地方，欢迎试用反馈。

> 來源提供的正文:
> 最近在折腾 AI 图生视频，自己做了一个小工具站 PicTempo，刚上线，来 V2EX 分享一下。
>
> 网站：https://photo2video.org
>
> 做这个工具的起因是，之前给网站制作展示素材时，经常需要把图片转成视频。
>
> 实际用下来发现几个问题：同一张图片、同样的提示词，生成结果可能差别很大。有时候只有镜头在移动，人物基本不动；固定镜头后，视频又容易显得很死板。
>
> 另外，有些时候只是想把几张照片合成一个视频，并不需要 AI 生成，但不少工具也要注册或者付费。
>
> 所以就尝试把这两类需求放在一个网站里。
>
> **目前主要做了几个功能：**
>
> 1. **免费照片合成视频**：支持 2–24 张照片，可以调整顺序、时长、转场、画面比例和背景音乐，直接导出 MP4，不需要登录、不消耗积分，也不添加网站水印。
> 2. **AI 图片转视频**：上传图片，通过动作提示词描述人物或者镜头的运动，生成动态视频。这部分还在持续优化生成效果。
> 3. **批量图片动画**：设计了批量处理模式，希望能够一次上传多张图片，减少重复操作。
>
> 还加了一个手机扫码上传图片的功能，电脑端打开网站后，可以直接使用手机选图。
>
> 目前最花时间的其实不是做页面，而是生成效果和实际使用体验。尤其是如何让人物动作自然、镜头有层次感，同时尽量保留原图细节。
>
> 网站还处于早期阶段，很多地方需要完善。
>
> **想请 V 友帮忙看看：**
>
> - 这样的工具更需要 AI 图片动画，还是免费的照片合成视频？
> - 页面操作流程有没有不直观或者多余的地方？
> - 示例视频的质量和展示方式是否足够直观？
>
> 欢迎直接提意见，尤其是体验不好的地方。
>
> 感谢大家！

> 很多 CLI 的 `FAILED` 在终端里就是一行普通文本。颜色是程序自己输出的，终端只负责渲染；程序不标红，终端不会替它标。我的旧配置管着提示符、`ls` 和 `git diff`，管不到程序输出。四个 tab 一起跑的时候，找报错只能靠 Ctrl+F 或肉眼扫。 原来那套配置我用了五年，是按「敲命令」的节奏长的：一条命令跑几秒，输出十几行。现在一个 agent 任务跑几分钟，输出几百行，终端…

> 來源提供的正文:
> 很多 CLI 的 `FAILED` 在终端里就是一行普通文本。颜色是程序自己输出的，终端只负责渲染；程序不标红，终端不会替它标。我的旧配置管着提示符、`ls` 和 `git diff`，管不到程序输出。四个 tab 一起跑的时候，找报错只能靠 Ctrl+F 或肉眼扫。
>
> 原来那套配置我用了五年，是按「敲命令」的节奏长的：一条命令跑几秒，输出十几行。现在一个 agent 任务跑几分钟，输出几百行，终端从执行窗口变成了监控面板。需求变了，配置没跟上。
>
> 改动都发生在 iTerm2 这一层：Triggers、全局键映射、Smart Selection。换哪个 CLI 都生效。
>
> ## 一、日志关键词染色
>
> Profile 里带了 4 条 Triggers：
>
> - `ERROR|ERRORS|FATAL|FAILED|FAILURE|PANIC|Exception` → 错误色
> - `WARN|WARNING|DEPRECATED|TODO|FIXME` → 警告色
> - `SUCCESS|SUCCEEDED|SUCCESSFUL|PASSED` → 成功色
> - `Password:` / `Passphrase:` 提示 → 直接弹 iTerm2 密码管理器
>
> 匹配到只标那个词，不整行涂色；高亮色取自当前主题的语义色，换肤时跟着变，不用改规则。
>
> Triggers 只对**新开的 tab** 生效，装完不 `Cmd+T` 会以为没生效。另外正则是笨的，日志里出现 `ERROR` 但实际是正常文本也会标。我接受这个误报，因为漏报更烦。
>
> ## 二、Shift+Enter 换行不提交
>
> iTerm2 的 `GlobalKeyMap` 加 Shift+Enter 映射，同一按键按新旧 iTerm2 的格式各写一份：`0xd-0x20000` 和 `0xd-0x20000-0x24`，新版多一个键码。按下去发的是换行，不是回车，写给 AI 的多行 prompt 不用先开编辑器，也不怕中途误提交。
>
> 映射内容放在一个 JSON 数据文件里，安装时读进 iTerm2，不写死在脚本里；卸载只摘掉这两条键映射，不动你自己的其它映射。
>
> ## 三、语义 Cmd-click
>
> `path:line`、Git SHA、`localhost:port` 走 iTerm2 的 Smart Selection，Cmd-click 分别打开编辑器、跑 `git show`、开浏览器。这条和 Triggers 一样，只在 iTerm2 里有，Ghostty 没有对应物。
>
> ## 为什么不做 agent 插件
>
> Claude Code 有自己的输出格式，Codex 有另一套。写解析插件等于给每个工具各写一遍，还得跟着它们升级。放在终端层，所有输出一视同仁，这是选它的原因。
>
> 代价是只能做正则和键映射，理解不了语义；误报、只对新 tab 生效、绑定 iTerm2，这些我认。要更聪明的解析，就得回到 agent 那一层做，两边不是替代关系。
>
> 配色这次不展开。免费版是 MIT，3 套社区配色和上面这些 iTerm2 设置都在里面；品牌主题、场景、工作区、光学校准属于付费档，范围写在官网。
>
> ## 怎么复现
>
> ```bash
> git clone https://github.com/huiyonghkw/hekouwang-terminal-lite-skill.git
> cd hekouwang-terminal-lite-skill
> ./scripts/install.sh --dry-run   # 先看改哪些文件、写哪些设置
> HKW_ASSUME_YES=1 ./scripts/install.sh
> ```
>
> 已经有自己 `.zshrc` 的，先 `./scripts/migrate.sh` 看报告，再 `--apply`；`install.sh` 会先备份再覆盖。脚本装 Homebrew / oh-my-zsh 前会把官方安装脚本下载到临时文件并打印 SHA-256；上面命令里的 `HKW_ASSUME_YES=1` 就是「我已确认来源」的开关。
>
> 装完先 `./scripts/doctor.sh --status`，看主题、Node、语义层钉住没有。换肤先 `./scripts/theme.sh --plan tokyo-night`，它只列出会改哪些文件，不写盘；确认后再去掉 `--plan`。
>
> ## 边界
>
> Triggers 和 Cmd-click 是 iTerm2 独有，换终端就没有。只支持 macOS。安装脚本还会装 Homebrew、oh-my-zsh 和 `eza` / `bat` / `delta` / `fzf` 这套 CLI，但那属于 shell 环境，跟帖子里这三个 iTerm2 设置是两件事。
>
> 如果只是想让 tab 好认，先别装，给每个 tab 改名字和颜色成本更低。这套东西解决的是日志染色、多行输入和换机迁移，不适合所有人。
>
> 仓库：https://github.com/huiyonghkw/hekouwang-terminal-lite-skill
> 官网：https://huiyonghkw.github.io/hekouwang-terminal-lite-skill/?lang=zh
>
> 有问题在这帖回，或者开 issue。特别是 Triggers 的正则，欢迎拿你们的日志来砸，误报多了我再收窄。

> 來源提供的正文:
> 各位 V 友大家好，之前在这里分享过我做的 macOS 应用切换工具 AbcTab（给 ⌘-Tab 加上首字母直达、同字母轮切、多窗口展开和乒乓模式）。
>
> 今天刚发布了 v1.5.0，这次的核心更新是：双击修饰键唤起（停留过滤模式），有 V 友之前提到过。
>
> 之前 AbcTab 沿用的是经典 ⌘-Tab 按住维持的交互，单字母跳转很快，但在两种场景下还是有点累：
>
> 开了一堆同首字母应用（比如 Chrome / Cursor / Codex / Calendar），按住 ⌘ 连按好几下 C 手指有点别扭；
> 只是想随手切个应用，不想左手一直死按着修饰键不放。
>
> **产品官网： [](https://solocraft.app/zh/abctab**)
>
> 不直接送激活码了，之前发了不少，激活也就一半多点。14 天免费体验，足够长了。如果体验之后觉得好，可以分享下体验新的，送激活码。
>
> App 也上架了 Mac App Store 集成了绝大部分功能，但因为沙箱的限制，只能使用 ⌥-Tab 来切换，也不支持多窗口。跳转到 (Mac App Store)[https://apps.apple.com/cn/app/abctab/id6830197687?l=en-GB&mt=12]，1.5.0 正在审核中。
>
> ---
>
> **1.5.0 新增：双击修饰键 + 停留过滤模式**
>
> 在「设置 → 进阶」里新增了独立卡片（默认关闭，完全不影响原有习惯）：
>
> - 左 / 右 / 任意修饰键独立区分 支持左 / 右 / 任意 ⌘、⌥、⌃ 共 9 种组合。我自己设的是 右 ⌘ 双击，左手完全解放，也不会和日常 ⌘+C / ⌘+V 冲突。双击松手后切换面板会停留在屏幕上。
>
> - 多字母 / 缩写 / 拼音过滤，底层绕过输入法 面板停留后直接敲 a-z / 0-9 过滤当前运行的应用（按 MRU 顺序排列）：
>
>     - 英文/数字前缀：cu → Cursor、1p → 1Password
>     - 词首与驼峰缩写：vsc → Visual Studio Code、gc → Google Chrome、wc → WeChat
>     - 中文拼音首字母与全拼前缀：wx / weix → 微信
>     - 专门处理了输入法拦截，哪怕当前开着中文拼音输入法，直接打字也不会弹出系统拼音候选框。
>
> - 唯一匹配 0ms 秒切，过滤结果一收敛到 1 个应用，不需要再按回车，0ms 直接切过去（比如双击右 ⌘ → 敲 wc 瞬间切到微信）。如果不喜欢自动切，设置里也有子开关可以关掉，改成回车/空格手动确认。

### [\[开源\] Peerdeck：macOS / iOS 原生 qBittorrent / Transmission/Flood 遥控，多服务器、多站点 PT 管理](https://www.v2ex.com/t/1259246)

`v2ex:create` · T2 · 2026-11-23 13:06 UTC · zh-CN · by birdplane

> Vibe 了一个自己用的一个小工具，开源了：Peerdeck，macOS 和 iOS 原生 qBittorrent / Transmission / Flood 遥控。 解决的问题：服务器不止一台、站点不止一个时，网页后台来回切很烦，失效种清理又怕误删交叉做种的数据。 功能： - 所有服务器一个列表，按状态 / 服务器 / 站点 / 分类 / 标签过滤，批量操作 - 按站点看上传 / 下载 / 总…

> 來源提供的正文:
> Vibe 了一个自己用的一个小工具，开源了：Peerdeck，macOS 和 iOS 原生 qBittorrent / Transmission / Flood 遥控。
>
> 解决的问题：服务器不止一台、站点不止一个时，网页后台来回切很烦，失效种清理又怕误删交叉做种的数据。
>
> 功能：
> - 所有服务器一个列表，按状态 / 服务器 / 站点 / 分类 / 标签过滤，批量操作
> - 按站点看上传 / 下载 / 总量；被站点删除、Tracker 拒绝、连不上 Tracker 的种子单独列出，一键清理，交叉做种仍在用的数据会保留
> - Mac 上批量换 Tracker 域名 / passkey，每个站点设默认服务器
> - 菜单栏看速度，下载完成通知
> - 直连客户端，中间没有服务器，自己不下载不做种；支持多地址（局域网 / 组网 / DDNS / 反代）、自签证书，密码存钥匙串
> - 单服务器测过 2 万个种子
>
> 安装，macOS 15+：
> ```
> brew tap xheiop/peerdeck https://github.com/xheiop/Peerdeck
> brew install --cask xheiop/peerdeck/peerdeck
> ```
>
> iOS 17+ 只能侧载或者巨魔（AltStore / SideStore，README 里有源）。
>
> 地址：https://github.com/xheiop/Peerdeck

>
> 我目前是大二正在学体系结构
>
> 准备过几个月直接用chisel做个rtl核心一直做到跑通linux之类的在fpga
>
> 因为我目前还没学完
>
> 也是双非财经学校
>
> 没有任何的实验室和导师 纯靠自己的自驱力和兴趣
>
> 我目前学到的大部分都是数学方程的约束
>
> 我目前对芯片架构设计和体系结构的认知就是
>
> 这玩意很多都是数学
>
> 需要写下很多布尔控制方程和状态转移来约束
>
> 当然也需要考虑实际上的时序问题上板子一些功耗什么的一些现实的约束
>
> 所以未来ai一定会大力推进芯片架构设计
>
> 但是我知道芯片研发周期是很长的
>
> ai如果在软件里越迭代
>
> 硬件的研发周期不会等
>
> 同时还需要人类的审核
>
> 比如你车载芯片出问题了撞车死人必须要找到追责
>
> 在人类仍需要担责的一段时间
>
> 我不清楚这个方向还能活多久
>
> 如果活不下来我依然会继续学完弄完我的fpga就当纯粹满足求知欲了
>
> 或者这个与具身智能交叉一下
>
> 给机器人做芯片
>
> 会能接触到更多脏现实吗
>
> 我也知道这个行业需要预测未来 博弈现实中的很多因素
>
> 我觉得
>
> 坐在屏幕前的理论研究能力在新社会估值大幅下降
>
> 而承担风险 物理直觉 多维现实博弈 预测未来这些能力的估值会大幅提升
>
> 个人简洁难免有误 期望佬友点明小友一二
>
> 欢迎讨论

### [【开源推广】语阅 Yuyue：用 Rust + 原生界面写的本地看书、听书软件，免登录无广告](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230375)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-23 16:08 UTC · zh-CN · by 停留在

> https://linux.do#p-25150142-h-1本帖使用社区开源推广，符合推广要求。我申明并遵循社区要求的以下内容：
>
> 我的帖子已经打上 [开源推广](https://linux.do/tag/2234-tag/2234) 标签： 是
>
> 我的开源项目完整开源，无未开源部分： 是
>
> 我的开源项目已链接认可 LINUX DO 社区： 是
>
> 我帖子内的项目介绍，AI生成、润色内容部分已截图发出： 是
>
> 以上选择我承诺是永久有效的，接受社区和佬友监督： 是
>
> 以下为项目介绍正文内容，AI生成、润色内容已使用截图方式发出
>
> ---
>
> 各位佬友，分享一个自己写的免费开源本地看书、听书软件「语阅 Yuyue」。免登录、无广告、无后台服务器，书和笔记都留在本地。
>
> 主要功能：
>
> 本地看书与管书：支持 EPUB / PDF / TXT / MOBI，支持 Wi-Fi 传书、直连 NAS（Calibre OPDS / WebDAV），做了中文排版优化与多套阅读纸张。
>
> 边看边听无缝切换：书页里点哪句就从哪句开始念，自动跟读翻页，停下接着看还在同一行；自带免配置自然人声和 125MB 离线语音包，也支持接豆包、OpenAI 等接口。
>
> 小说广播剧模式：支持开启多角色广播剧朗读，自动或手动给书里不同人物分配不同声音、搭配环境音（接上大模型可辅助识别每句台词是谁说的）。
>
> 听播客与有声书：支持 RSS 订阅播客、导入有声书，听的时候也能对照内容随时划线记笔记。
>
> 外文查词与防剧透问答：内置离线词典，点词查释义、双击翻整句；可连本机 Ollama 或 DeepSeek 问书中细节，默认只读已看章节不剧透。
>
> 笔记导出与网盘同步：划线和想法一键导出 Markdown、带划线 EPUB，或发往 Obsidian / Notion / flomo / Anki；多设备走你自己的 iCloud 或 WebDAV 同步（Google Drive 即将支持）。
>
> 适合谁用：
>
> 平时自己存电子书或用 NAS 管书、看小说想听多角色广播剧、读英文原著，或者习惯把笔记留在 Obsidian 里的佬友。
>
> 技术实现：
>
> 跨端核心：Rust + SQLite（负责书籍解析、中英断句、本地检索与多端同步）
>
> 各端界面：Apple 端 SwiftUI，Android 端 Kotlin + Jetpack Compose，开发中的 Windows 端 WinUI 3 / C#
>
> 排版与语音：书页排字与高亮用 TypeScript 跑在系统自带 WebView 里，离线朗读基于本地 ONNX 语音模型，安装包小、启动和翻页都比较轻快
>
> 目前状态与还在完善的地方：
>
> 刚发 0.1.0 第一版，Mac（Apple 芯片） 和 Android 可直接在 Releases 下载安装包（Mac 未签开发者证书，首次打开在「隐私与安全性」点一次“仍要打开”即可）。目前 Windows 版还在开发中，*iOS 版**暂未上架商店需自签 `.ipa`；另外 广播剧角色识别与配音效果、有声书自动对齐、书房电台也还在继续打磨完善。
>

### [【开源推广】从 grill-me 生长出的工作流](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230360)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-23 16:03 UTC · zh-CN · by kakarot8

> 本帖使用社区开源推广，符合推广要求。我申明并遵循社区要求的以下内容：
>
> 我的帖子已经打上 开源推广 标签： 是
>
> 我的开源项目完整开源，无未开源部分： 是
>
> 我的开源项目已链接认可 LINUX DO 社区： 是
>
> 我帖子内的项目介绍，AI生成、润色内容部分已截图发出： 是
>
> 以上选择我承诺是永久有效的，接受社区和佬友监督： 是
>
> 以下为项目介绍正文内容，AI生成、润色内容已使用截图方式发出
>
> 项目地址：
>
> 上游 grow-me：[GitHub - Trunks820/grow-me: 让需求长成方案：本机网页逐轮澄清需求，回答开花、追问长枝、复核黄叶、按章结果。 · GitHub](https://github.com/Trunks820/grow-me)
>
> 下游 grow-loop：[GitHub - Trunks820/grow-loop: 让方案长成交付：面向 AI 编程 Agent 的零依赖多包交付状态机（2+2+2 自动升级与刹车、跨宿主接力、零凭据托管、脱敏证据包）。 · GitHub](https://github.com/Trunks820/grow-loop)
>
> 工作流痛点：
>
> 站里不少佬友应该都用过matt的 grill-me系列的skill —— 让 AI 别急着写代码，先一轮一轮把隐藏分支拷问清楚。
>
> 他这一套我自己拿过来修修改改，做成了自己的一个工作流，中大型需求过来了先读代码后拷打，最后出一个包含设计方案 / 开发清单 的HTML。但在实际用下来后会发现几个问题：
>
> grill-me拷打过几轮后，AI现在倒是不会忘记前面的决策，瓶颈反而是我自己：拷打轮次一旦过多，谁依赖谁早看花眼了；中途推翻之前的一个决定，前面那些回答作废就只能全靠我翻了；而且最最最容易的是后面的问题全都会变成按建议走/按你推荐的来 ![:rofl:](https://cdn.ldstatic.com/images/emoji/twemoji/rofl.png?v=16)
>
> grill-with-docs呢，这个倒是会帮你记下来决策，但是每一批拷打完后会写一下md，搭配 gpt简直慢出天际，嗯，特别是GPT不说人话，导致我需要反复琢磨的时候，真的是双重折磨！
>
> html产物的初衷是好的，方便人看（以前是生成MD放在Obsidian，前面我还有兴趣看，后面工期紧多项目并行我就不看了），但是由于没有约束，gpt写了一堆编号并且附带上代码位置，导致读起来很费劲，有一段时间也没看了；后面就是让claude优化了一版，改为三视图（新增验收标准，可写验收方案），并且把开发清单改造成一个一个的任务包，方便让不同的AI按照包来执行。
>
> grow-me实机演示
>
> 所以我顺着 grill-me 长出了两个开源skill工作流，刚把上下游拍板原话交接彻底接通。先看一遍完整实机流程动图：
>
> ![grow-me-full-flow](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/a/c/4/ac4d259644cf130fde114b58aa75d77502517f50.webp)
>
> grow-me的构思
>
> 第一是不想做在对话框一直被拷问，大脑上下文处理不过来；
>
> 第二又不想在web页面上做成表单样式，感觉很low；
>
> 第三就是突然想到了植物大战僵尸世界树的生长，每喂一包饲料就会长大一点。这个也是grow-me诞生的主要来源
>
> grow-loop的介绍
>
> 后续我在codex里面指定 grok、dsh、gemini 来开发不同的任务包后发现，几个指定AI开发的skill没有统一规矩，经常会返工速度也提不起来，大多数时候还不如我复制每一包任务的提示词过去给他们开发。 所以才有了下游的 grow-loop。
>
> grow-loop 是在用上 grow-me 拿出html产物后，可以直接在当前harness里面执行/grow-loop 来做Host总控， 你可以和它聊一聊每包任务的开发者，审查者这些，指定好后可以直接一路开发到需求完成，除非有敏感操作才会停下来
>
> grow-loop防护治理
>
> 在开发loop的时候，我是拿真实需求来直接跑的，碰到过几次问题，
>
> 比如有一个复杂的需求让ds4.1f开发的时候，一直返工修复，修了两轮还没好我立马中断让gpt接手开发了，一轮过了。这次问题产出一个规矩：修两轮还是不通过后，会自动升档，升档后的模型如果修复两轮还是没好的话，会停下来问你，不会一直派发修改。
>
> 错题本（实验ing）：另外我还加了个实验性的错题本机制——失败先存草稿，人工确认规则后才写进后续任务书，目前只过了自动化单测，目前没有新需求来做实测过效果了，欢迎各位佬友试试！
>
> [![06-user-workflow-chart](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/e/4/b/e4b2f31765e105e0a64a8235335d1efc44985794_2_690x463.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/e/4/b/e4b2f31765e105e0a64a8235335d1efc44985794.png)
>
> 依旧碎碎念
>
> 我自己平时在 codex、agy、cc上跑，主要是cc，跑的比较顺畅，指哪打哪的感觉很舒服
>
> 哪步用着别扭或者踩了坑，欢迎各位佬友反馈
>
> 后续升级的方向比较大，不知道一个人能不能做出来，尽力而为吧
>
> ps：云途也马上准备发一个新版，最近优化了不少东西，个人感觉还不错
>
> 实机交互与 grow-me 生成的产物三视图截图 [（点击了解更多详细信息）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230360/1)

### [深度体验4neon和4hydrogen几天的感受](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230330)

`linuxdo:开发调优` · T2 · 2026-11-23 15:53 UTC · zh-CN · by SwiftUI

> 深度用了三四天(主要是neon，之前carbon也用了不过没用太多)，说说在我几个真实项目下使用的感受
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/f/c/d/fcd37228eb0e035a4ab2f8abc222f773faaafbfa_2_639x500.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/f/c/d/fcd37228eb0e035a4ab2f8abc222f773faaafbfa.png)
>
> https://linux.do#p-25149730-h-1省流
>
> neon
>
> 普通任务体感比类似价格的opus5.5要强，比gpt理解需求能力更强更自主，如果任务是普通业务逻辑开发，不涉及创意类似乎可以完美平替opus和sol
>
> 考虑到羊毛的话挺划算 没有羊毛正价的话考虑到他的雷霆效率额度不是很友好
>
> neon能力上限不是很高 复杂任务表现下感觉逻辑略强opus5.5但是ui更差，总体完成度略逊6.2sol 可以看后面案例截图 测试了几个场景
>
> hydrogen
>
> 很快，能力也不弱，但是有3.8f一样的毛病(自信编造数据，压缩丢目标，一直读文件不写东西，《你说的对》) 长上下文的稳定性似乎不如ds4.1f 感觉更适合问答用
>
> 说下我测试的案例：
>
> 第一个是clean-room复刻一个声音合成引擎 感兴趣的可以看下这个(https://linux.do/t/topic/3146382)
>
> agent环境：ZCode
>
> 提供工具：完整命令访问权限,IDA MCP
>
> 任务给他之前的状态是让ds和免费的hy4flash干了两整天的结果（已经让hy4f和ds4.1f把声库都解密了，然后给了几个工程文件以及对应渲染结果，并且ds和hy4f已经还原一部分的算法 让他继续还原一个渲染引擎 因为ds4.1f和hy4f实在是干不好了 当然这两个模型也很神奇有空了说一下）
>
> 首先说下最终成果 经过斗志斗勇一整天总算是差不多了，基本上功能正常了，只剩下了几个参数解析的小问题导致的结果问题，但是过程中发现的问题也不少
>
> https://linux.do#p-25149730-h-4hydrogen-24hydrogen在 本次任务 中的问题
>
> 本来想着ds和hy4都能整点名堂4hy速度那么快应该效果更好 但是实测下来就是不回复一直干 忽略上下文大小导致完全无法使用（是的他压缩了两次写入0文件0记忆 全程都是在调用ida mcp去看汇编和反汇编，win32api的符号也不导入，常见函数结构也不知道改改名记录下）
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/5/b/e/5be3353d8746c9560ad52d5cb91aeb211ca66f52.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/5/b/e/5be3353d8746c9560ad52d5cb91aeb211ca66f52.png)
>
> 于是这个任务4hy算是废了 直接切到4neon 继续测
>
> https://linux.do#p-25149730-h-4neon-34neon的优点
>
> 1.相比gemini的其他模型（包括carbon），4neon的agent能力明显提高（有点像ds4到4.1的那种提升），比如压缩后能正确调用工具而不是疯狂写脚本操作，以及长任务每个操作阶段会阶段性总结而不是一直调工具
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/0/3/703b9a7d485d5f747c287264d32d73f3a35ffd62.png)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/0/3/703b9a7d485d5f747c287264d32d73f3a35ffd62.png)
>

>
> hydrogen就是出现了压缩之后不会用工具的问题，以及速度非常慢的问题（莫名其妙分段读文件，可能是agy里面会截断导致训练的数据偏差，以及一直读文件不写导致压缩后丢进度）
>
> https://linux.do#p-25149730-h-10总结
>
> 4 Hydrogen还是有3.8的老毛病，但是比3.8强点并且速度更快了，可以考虑用来干杂活，复杂任务会导致即使500k上下文也会疯狂压缩无法推进任务（考虑到这玩意300tps的输出，感觉额度掉的速度和用neon差不多了）
>
> 4 Neon能力挺强，agent应该是gemini系列最强的，但是明显能力上限不够，在各个复杂场景下测试都有或多或少的问题
>
> 知识面很广，意图理解很好，用于planner和当“gpt提示词生成器”应该效果非常好，而且中低难度的活干起来也都没有问题，相比3.8f和4hy强多了 最大缺点可能是正价agy用下来额度其实不算多（如果考虑到感人的执行效率其实干不了几个任务 当然可能是我给的任务都比较难）
>
> 4hy个人感觉不适合做子代理（可能思考开低点有改善） 在使用4neon派发子代理的时候，简单任务给hydrogen，复杂任务给neon，每次都是neon先完成并且验收没问题，然后hydrogen一直卡着（疯狂读文件-压缩-rg搜文件-压缩-py读文件-压缩），最后是子代理直接给结束了然后自己搞 所以如果额度充足不如全用neon省事 速度还更快

### [服务器平台 FinPro](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230226)

`linuxdo:搞七捻三` · T2 · 2026-11-23 15:30 UTC · zh-CN · by guan09

> 避雷「玖云FinPro」：60元退款审核近两个月，客服不仅业务一塌糊涂，还直接扣帽子威胁用户
>
> (注：配图已隐去所有个人信息)
>
> 在这家云服务商续费服务器后，踩了一连串离谱的坑。目前60元退款在平台卡了快两个月还在“审核中”，整个售后过程更是让人大开眼界：
>
> 1. 没IP照样扣费，客服瞎排查浪费两小时 续费后发现后台IP直接显示为空（null），本地SSH根本连不上。找客服反馈，对方连账号状态都不核实，张口就甩锅给“系统推送框架更新有Bug”，让我干等了两个多小时。最后才查出来，是因为我逾期24小时续费，原节点的IP早被回收分给别人了。合着手里已经没IP了，系统还能照常扣钱，直接塞给我一台连不上的空壳机器。
>
> 2. 业务能力堪忧，“配置带宽”和“跨境网速”都分不清 因为原节点缺货，客服主动提出帮我免费迁移到其他支持海外访问的节点。我明确表示旧数据不要了，只要求新机器的套餐带宽规格（25Mbps/100Mbps）别缩水。结果客服完全理解不了，硬把“服务器配置带宽”曲解成“保证国内连海外的实际网速”，反过来质问我：“国内跑海外谁能给你保证？”连最基础的行业概念都搞混，沟通极其费劲。
>
> 3. 擅自退回平台余额，单方面强制结单 前面明明说好了由客服帮我操作迁移，我等着就行。结果对方连个招呼都不打，直接把钱退进了平台余额（根本不原路退回），随后单方面关闭工单，让我自己重新去选配置、重新下单。合着钱不仅套在平台里提不出来，还得我自己收拾烂摊子。
>
> 4. 态度极其恶劣，拿“犯罪”和“监管部门”恐吓用户 我质疑他们出尔反尔、推卸责任，客服非但没有半点歉意，反而直接说出“我帮你是不是协助你犯罪呢”这种令人作呕的话，接着指责我在外发帖黑他们，最后甚至甩出“保留所有服务器日志配合监管部门调查”来威胁恐吓。
>
> 花钱买服务器，结果机器用不了、退款卡两月，最后还要挨客服一顿威胁。想买他家机器的，建议慎重。
>
> 图片 [（点击了解更多详细信息）](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230226/1)

### [写了个小工具：让 5 个 Harness 只显示模型真正支持的思考档位](https://linux.do/t/topic/3230185)

`linuxdo:资源荟萃` · T2 · 2026-11-23 15:25 UTC · zh-CN · by lxgy1024

> https://linux.do#p-25148750-h-1本帖使用社区开源推广，符合推广要求。我申明并遵循社区要求的以下内容：
>
> 我的帖子已经打上 [开源推广](https://linux.do/tag/2234-tag/2234) 标签： 是
>
> 我的开源项目完整开源，无未开源部分： 是
>
> 我的开源项目已链接认可 LINUX DO 社区： 是
>
> 我帖子内的项目介绍，AI生成、润色内容部分已截图发出： 是
>
> 以上选择我承诺是永久有效的，接受社区和佬友监督： 是
>
> 本项目解决这样的问题：网关转发 DeepSeek，官方文档 reasoning_effort 只有 low / high / max，而 medium / xhigh 都会被映射成 high，然而OpenCode 默认给 low/medium/high，网关生成的 Codex catalog 写成 low/medium/high/xhigh 虽然可以映射，但是 max 就选不到了。
>
> 本项目思路是：给网关发一个非法的 effort，读它 400 里的 valid levels:
>
> Anthropic 协议就用 output_config.effort 去试。
>
> 如果网关对 bogus 都返回 200，就标成 no-validation，最后用 models.dev 的声明
>
> 做了一个 core CLI + 五个宿主插件，都放在
>
> 仓库

This report adds that the `noglob` workaround is incomplete, and asks for a way to get plain Microsoft C runtime parsing, or for documentation. Companion report, same code path: #6516 (arguments cut at 8,186 characters).
>

> ```
> git version 2.55.0.windows.3
> cpu: x86_64
> built from commit: 52ca1113d651127f89477a8763f86ab20f645e1d

> MSYS runtime: `MSYS_NT-10.0-19045 3.6.9-b4195d69.x86_64 2026-06-06 17:49 UTC x86_64 Msys`. Not run on 2.56.0.windows.3 (the newest release); the code on `main` of git-for-windows/msys2-runtime (read 2026-10-25) has the same logic.

>
> Not relevant: it reproduces by starting `usr\bin\printf.exe` directly.

> ### Terminal/shell
>
> PowerShell 7.6.7, and Python 3.14 `subprocess.run`: any parent that is not an MSYS program.
>
> ### Commands that trigger the issue
>
> PowerShell quotes the argument for the Microsoft C runtime (`"a\\b c"`), under which the two backslashes are literal because no quote follows them:
>
> ```powershell
> $e = 'C:\Program Files\Git\usr\bin\printf.exe'
> & $e '<%s>\n' 'a\\b c'              # prints <a\b c>; expected <a\\b c>
> $env:MSYS = 'noglob'
> & $e '<%s>\n' 'a\\b c'              # prints <a\\b c>
> & $e '<%s>\n' 'say "hi" there'      # prints <say \hi\ there>; expected <say "hi" there>
> ```
>
> Python's `subprocess.list2cmdline` produces the same command lines. What arrives (default / with `MSYS=noglob`):
>
> | argument sent | default | `MSYS=noglob` |
> |---|---|---|
> | `a\\b c` (2 backslashes) | `a\b c` | `a\\b c` |
> | `a\\\b c` (3) | `a\\b c` | `a\\\b c` |
> | `a\\\\\\b c` (6) | `a\\\b c` | `a\\\\\\b c` |
> | `say "hi" there` | `say "hi" there` | `say \hi\ there` |
> | `a\"b c` | `a\"b c` | two arguments: `a\\\b` and `c` |
>
> ### Expected behaviour
>
> Either a way to start an MSYS program with its command line parsed by Microsoft C runtime rules (as `CommandLineToArgvW` does: a backslash is literal unless a quote follows), or documentation that says which convention applies.
>
> ### Actual behaviour
>
> For a non-MSYS parent with globbing on (the default), `quoted()` in `winsup/cygwin/dcrt0.cc` keeps the quotes and `globify` treats a backslash as an escape, so each run of backslashes is halved (n becomes ceil(n/2)). `MSYS=noglob` switches to a different quote handling that keeps the backslashes but does not understand `\"` inside a quoted argument (rows 4 and 5). So no setting gives the convention that PowerShell and Python's `list2cmdline` write here (and, per anthropics/claude-code#92543, Node's libuv).
>
> ### Other interesting things
>
> Requests, in order of preference: (1) make `noglob` keep `\"` as an escaped quote inside quoted arguments, so it becomes a complete workaround; (2) an `MSYS` option that parses the inbound command line with Microsoft C runtime rules, without globbing or `~` expansion; (3) at least document the convention and `noglob` for programs that start Git's `bash.exe` or MSYS tools.
>
> Seen in the wild: Claude Code's Bash tool on Windows halves backslash pairs in every command it runs through `bash.exe -c`, which silently changes regexes, JSON and Windows paths in agent-written scripts (anthropics/claude-code#85856, with 16 comments and a plain-Node reproduction in #92543). I have not tested Cygwin or MSYS2 proper.

> # Bug report: Bash tool silently halves backslashes on Windows (Git Bash / MSYS2…)
>
> ## Summary
>
> On Windows with Git Bash, every run of backslashes in a Bash tool command is
> halved before bash parses anything: `n` backslashes arrive as `ceil(n/2)`.
> Quoting cannot prevent it — single quotes, double quotes and quoted heredocs
> (`<<'EOF'`) are all affected identically, because the corruption happens at
> process-spawn time, before bash lexes a single character.
>
> Cause: Claude Code encodes its command line with **MSVCRT** quoting rules, but
> the target (`bash.exe`) is an **MSYS2** binary that decodes with a different
> convention. MSYS2 performs an un-escaping pass that Claude Code never escaped
> for, so one backslash is eaten from every pair.
>
> ## Severity
>
> Two failure modes, and the second is the concerning one:
>
> ```python
> # loud - fails immediately
> "C:\\Users\\x"  ->  "C:\Users\x"  ->  SyntaxError: (unicode error)
>                                       truncated \UXXXXXXXX escape
>
> # SILENT - exit code 0, wrong result
> print("a\\nb")  ->  print("a\nb")  ->  prints a real newline
> ```
>
> Single backslashes survive, so raw-string regexes like `r"\s+"` keep working.
> That masks the bug until a Windows path or a literal escape appears, and it
> means agents can produce silently wrong output with no diagnostic.
>
> This affects any heredoc'd or inlined content containing backslashes — Python,
> sed, awk, jq, LaTeX — not just Python.
>
> ## Environment
>
> - Windows 11 Home 10.0.26200
> - Claude Code 2.1.222 (`AppData\Roaming\Claude\claude-code\2.1.222\claude.exe`)
> - Git for Windows bash 5.3.15(1)-release, MSYS2 runtime 3.6.9
> - Python 3.13.14
>
> ## Reproduction A — through Claude Code
>
> Run as a Bash tool command:
>
> ```bash
> printf '%s\n' 'a\\b'
> ```
>
> - Expected: `a\\b` (bash single quotes are literal; nothing should change)
> - Actual: `a\b`
>
> ## Reproduction B — standalone, isolates the layer
>
> Does not involve Claude Code. Sends a byte-exact Windows command line from a
> native process, so nothing but MSYS2 can alter it:
>
> ```python
> import subprocess, re
>
> BASH = r"C:\Program Files\Git\bin\bash.exe"
> inner = r"printf '%s' 'A:\ B:\\ C:\\\ D:\\\\'"   # runs of 1,2,3,4
> cmdline = '"' + BASH + '" -c "' + inner + '"'
>
> out = subprocess.run(cmdline, capture_output=True).stdout.decode()
> print("sent    :", [len(s) for s in re.findall(r"\\+", inner)])
> print("received:", [len(s) for s in re.findall(r"\\+", out)])
> ```
>
> ```
> sent    : [1, 2, 3, 4]
> received: [1, 1, 2, 2]
> ```
>
> The payload is inside bash **single quotes**, where bash performs no
> processing whatsoever. The loss is therefore not bash's.
>
> ## Root cause
>
> Windows passes a command **string**, not an argv array, so spawner and spawnee
> must agree on how to parse it. They don't:
>
> | | convention for a double-quoted argument |
> |---|---|
> | Claude Code (and every native spawner: Node, PowerShell, CPython) | **MSVCRT**: backslashes literal, except doubled immediately before a quote |
> | `bash.exe` (MSYS2 runtime) | `\\` → `\`, `\"` → `"` |
>
> MSYS2 runs an extra un-escaping pass the sender never escaped for.
>
> Confirmed by reading the live command line of the spawned bash via
> `Get-CimInstance Win32_Process`. Claude Code's encoding is *correct MSVCRT* — a
> run of 4 backslashes before a quote was correctly emitted as 8. The mismatch is
> purely in which convention the receiver applies.
>
> The trigger is specifically **double-quoted** arguments. Bare arguments are
> untouched:
>
> | command line | MSYS2 bash | native MSVCRT receiver |
> |---|---|---|
> | bare `a\b a\\b a\\\b a\\\\b` | 1,2,3,4 ✓ | 1,2,3,4 ✓ |
> | quoted `"a\b" "a\\b" …` | **1,1,2,2** ✗ | 1,2,3,4 ✓ |
>
> Since the Bash tool's command contains spaces, it is always passed as one
> double-quoted `-c` argument — i.e. always in the failing cell.
>
> ## Proposed fix
>
> When the spawn target is an MSYS2/Cygwin binary, encode arguments for **its**
> convention rather than MSVCRT's:
>
> ```js
> // inside the double-quoted argument
> const msys2Encode = (arg) => arg.replace(/\\/g, '\\\\').replace(/"/g, '\\"');
> ```
>
> **Must be conditional on the target.** Applying this to a native Windows
> executable breaks it in the opposite direction: MSVCRT treats backslashes as
> literal, so `C:\Users` would arrive as `C:\\Users`.
>
> ### Verification of the proposed encoder
>
> Measured against the current MSVCRT encoding, same inputs, same invocation
> shape (including the `eval '...'` wrapper Claude Code uses):
>
> | test | current encoding | proposed encoding |
> |---|---|---|
> | 11-case behaviour battery | 4 failures | **0 failures** |
> | 800 fuzzed payloads (quotes, spaces, `$`, backtick, glob metachars) | 21 mismatches | **0 mismatches** |
> | non-ASCII (accents, CJK, Greek, emoji) | correct | correct |
> | quoted args with spaces, `python3 -c`, globbing | correct | correct |
>
> It is a strict improvement: every case that works today still works, and the
> backslash failures are fixed.
>
> ## What does not work
>
> `MSYS=noglob` restores backslashes but disables the *entire* quote-unescaping
> pass, including `\"`. Since a native spawner must encode inner quotes as `\"`,
> every command containing a double quote then breaks:
>
> ```
> echo "result: ok"              ->  result:
> python3 -c "print('hi there')" ->  bash: syntax error near unexpected token `('
> ```
>
> Please don't ship that as a workaround.
>
> ## Workaround for users
>
> Write the script to a file (the Write tool is byte-faithful) and run the file.
> The Write tool, the PowerShell tool, script files and bash→bash spawns are all
> unaffected; only the Windows→MSYS2 command line corrupts.
>

>           theshasha](https://github.com/theshasha)
>
> ### Description
>
> On Windows the shell tool runs `bash.exe -c <command>`. Git Bas…h (MSYS2) splits the Windows command line with its own rules, which don't match how Node/Bun quote arguments, so bash runs a slightly different command than the one the model wrote. It still exits 0, so nobody notices:
>
> - `\\` becomes `\` anywhere in the command, even inside single quotes and quoted heredocs (`<<'EOF'`)
> - quoted arguments longer than ~8K chars get truncated (the msys runtime globs them through a fixed 8192 buffer), so long heredocs fail with odd syntax errors
>
> This silently corrupts files written via heredoc, regexes and Windows paths. `MSYS=noglob` is not a workaround: it stops eating `\\` but then mis-splits on `\"` (msys2/msys2-runtime#178).
>
> Not the same as #15810, which is about unquoted `C:\Users` (bash's own escaping).
>
> ### Plugins
>
> none
>
> ### OpenCode version
>
> 2.0.32 (also current `v2` source)
>
> ### Steps to reproduce
>
> Plain Node/Bun spawn, the same way the shell tool does it:
>
> ```js
> import { spawnSync } from "child_process"
> const bash = "C:/Program Files/Git/bin/bash.exe"
> const run = (cmd) => spawnSync(bash, ["-c", cmd], { encoding: "utf8" }).stdout
> console.log(run(String.raw`printf '%s\n' 'a\\b'`)) // prints a\b, expected a\\b
> console.log(run("cat <<'E' | wc -c\n" + "x".repeat(10000) + "\nE")) // prints 8169, expected 10001
> ```
>
> In OpenCode: use Git Bash as the shell and ask the agent to run `printf '%s\n' 'a\\b'`.
>
> Proposed fix: for MSYS2/Cygwin bash, pass the command in an environment variable and let bash `eval` it, so it never goes through the command line. I'll open a PR.
>
> ### Operating System
>
> Windows 11 (22621), Git for Windows 2.52.0
>

>
> n/a (shell tool)

> ### Issue for this PR
>
> Part of #57278 (fixes the backslash corruption; the 8K tr[…](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/57289)uncation is not addressed, see below)
>
> ### Type of change
>
> - [x] Bug fix
> - [ ] New feature
> - [ ] Refactor / code improvement
> - [ ] Documentation
>
> ### What does this PR do?
>
> Git Bash (MSYS2/Cygwin) splits its Windows command line with its own rules: inside the quotes Node/Bun add, `\\` collapses to `\`. So `bash -c <command>` silently changes commands with backslashes.
>
> `ShellSelect.args` now encodes the command for those rules: a leading space (bash ignores it; it guarantees the quotes and stops a leading `C:` from switching msys to DOS path rules), and backslash runs that Node doesn't double get doubled. The command is still the `-c` string, so nothing else changes: bash still execs the last command, timeout tree kill works as before, error messages are the same.
>
> Whether a bash is MSYS2/Cygwin is asked once per path with `echo $OSTYPE` and cached. The WSL launcher under `%SystemRoot%` is skipped (asking would boot WSL). With `noglob` in `MSYS`/`CYGWIN` the runtime splits differently, so the command is left as is there.
>
> Not fixed: quoted args over ~8K are still truncated by the msys runtime's glob buffer, and `noglob` can't carry `"` at all. Both need the command outside argv (env var, file, stdin), but then bash forks every command, and Cygwin's fork+exec detaches it from the Windows process tree, so taskkill /T on timeout leaves it running. I tried that first and backed it out; it needs MSYS-aware process cleanup first.
>
> ### How did you verify your code works?
>
> - New `shell-gitbash.test.ts` (Windows + Git Bash): backslashes/quotes/heredoc come through unchanged with the exit code kept; `noglob` leaves the command alone; a single command is killed with its shell on timeout. The first fails without the fix, the last fails with the env var approach.
> - Fuzzed the encoding against msys `printf.exe` under Node and Bun: 1544/1544 random and edge-case strings (quotes, backslash runs, drive letters, `@`, `~`, newlines, non-ASCII, up to ~8K) arrive unchanged.

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-23 14:32 UTC · zh-CN · by NANOPIM4

> [![2638f1f967ecc7d86d2479c6a2eb7eef](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/8/0/8/808521d5c84df8eb97ef35c5cf914538e6d7edc0_2_339x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/0/8/808521d5c84df8eb97ef35c5cf914538e6d7edc0.jpeg)
>
> [![4c8c1fd322f038c213aa118bf109bf0a](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/9/4/c/94c9056cf7d08b58ff81c3e1a8fd63d053bfdc70_2_500x500.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/9/4/c/94c9056cf7d08b58ff81c3e1a8fd63d053bfdc70.jpeg)
>
> NVIDIA宣布即日起恢复黄仁勋的总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务。此前，董事会因黄仁勋被列为外国情报目标而展开调查，在与美国政府高层沟通并确认其不构成国家安全风险后，董事会全票通过了复职决定。董事会主席哈维·琼斯表示对黄仁勋充满信心。黄仁勋对此表示荣幸，并将全力配合后续调查。同时，NVIDIA将成立国家安全与出口管制委员会，并增设首席合规官一职以强化贸易合规与安全管理。在此期间担任临时CEO的首席财务官科莱特·克雷斯将回归原有职责。英伟达股票盘前上涨30%。

> Google One 和 YouTube 促销优惠不得与其他优惠叠加使用，不可转让，也不能转售。Google 保留修改或取消任何优惠的权利，包括调整订阅方案价格。如果您取消后又决定重新订阅，可能就无法享受 Google One 和 YouTube 促销优惠了。如果您违反了 Google One 和 YouTube 促销活动条款及条件，将失去享受促销优惠的资格，我们将保留终止您的订阅的权利。
>
> 学生折扣优惠条款：
>
> 符合条件的学生可在促销期内试用并以折扣价订阅 Google AI Plus 和 Google AI Pro 方案（下称“学生优惠”）。学生优惠可能包括：延长试用期（在转为 Google AI Pro 付费包月方案后，可能随附 YouTube Premium Lite 福利）、Google AI Pro 包月方案折扣，或绑定 YouTube Premium 的 Google AI Pro 折扣套餐。YouTube Premium Lite 和 YouTube Premium 订阅使用的是个人账号，无法通过 Google One 家人群组共享。学生优惠不适用于学校分配的 Google Workspace 教育版账号。学生优惠仅适用于经认证的高等教育机构的全日制学生。如要符合享受这些学生优惠的条件，你必须在购买时通过第三方验证服务 SheerID 确认你的资格条件和学生身份，并且需要每年重新验证身份。你必须年满所在国家/地区的法定成年年龄，且在注册时所持 Google 账号须绑定有效 Google 支付资料。学生优惠在 Google One 及 YouTube 上最长可连续享受四年。若你的订阅时长超过 4 年，Google 保留取消或修改你所享学生优惠的权利。学生身份失效后，系统可能自动为你续订 Google AI Plus 或 Google AI Pro 方案，并按标准包月价格收费。在某些情况下，一旦不再符合学生资格条件，你的 Google One 折扣版方案就可能会到期。
>
> 需要关注的点有仨：

> 1.Google 保留修改或取消任何优惠的权利，包括调整订阅方案价格。
>
> 2.你必须在购买时通过第三方验证服务 SheerID 确认你的资格条件和学生身份，并且需要每年重新验证身份。

### [英伟达董事会恢复黄仁勋的总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务，随后股票暴力拉升30%+](https://linux.do/t/topic/3229810)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-23 14:20 UTC · zh-CN · by 🐟

> ![](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/media/sites/219/images/favicon.ico)
> [NVIDIA Newsroom](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/2/4/2/2427bdd93894bd4dc54919b3e0bdd729b00ff765_2_690x362.jpeg)
>
> [NVIDIA Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director](https://nvidianews.nvidia.com/news/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-president-ceo-and-board-director)
>
> NVIDIA (NASDAQ: NVDA) today announced that effective immediately, Jensen Huang has been reinstated as President and Chief Executive Officer and as a member of the Board.
>
> [!quote]+
>
> NVIDIA（纳斯达克股票代码：NVDA）今日宣布，即日起，黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）恢复担任公司总裁兼首席执行官，并重新加入董事会。在与黄仁勋先生进行了一系列讨论与沟通后，董事会一致投票决定让他回归；董事会对其坦诚的态度以及领导NVIDIA的能力表示认可。在做出此项决定过程中，董事会听取了美国政府高层的意见；基于这些反馈，董事会确信黄仁勋先生的回归不会构成任何国家安全风险。
>
> “董事会认为，黄仁勋是领导NVIDIA的最佳人选，他的回归符合公司股东、员工、合作伙伴及客户的最大利益，”董事会主席哈维·C·琼斯（Harvey C. Jones）表示，“我们对黄仁勋充满信心，并期待在他重掌公司领导权后与他携手共事。我们还要感谢科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）在担任临时首席执行官期间的出色表现，她也将继续履行其作为NVIDIA首席财务官的职责。”哈维·琼斯将继续担任董事会主席。
>
> “我很荣幸能回到NVIDIA，在这一新工业革命的开端，领导这家全球最具影响力的科技公司之一，”黄仁勋表示，“我怀着极其谦卑的心情承担起这一重任，并重申我的坚定承诺。感谢NVIDIA董事会在整个过程中给予的信任与审慎考量。我特别感谢哈维·琼斯作为董事会主席所展现出的领导力，也感谢科莱特·克雷斯以及我们的高管团队在这一期间对公司的引领。同时，我还要衷心感谢我们的员工、股东、业界领袖以及全球合作伙伴所给予的鼎力支持。最重要的是，感谢我家人的爱与支持。我已经迫不及待地想要重返工作岗位了。”
>
> 此前已有公告指出，鉴于近期有报道称黄仁勋先生曾成为外国情报活动的目标，董事会成立了一个完全由独立董事组成的委员会进行调查，并聘请了独立法律顾问协助开展此项调查。董事会重申，该委员会的调查工作将持续进行，直至得出最终结论。黄先生全力支持此次调查，并承诺将予以配合。
>
> 此外，董事会近期成立了一个“国家安全与出口管制委员会”，该委员会完全由独立董事组成，旨在监督贸易合规及国家安全风险。委员会正聘请在国家安全领域拥有丰富经验的法律顾问，这些顾问亦将引入具备相关专业知识的专家作为顾问。英伟达（NVIDIA）目前正着手招聘“首席合规官”这一新职位，负责监督公司整体的合规事务，并向提名与公司治理委员会汇报。英伟达将继续配合政府正在进行的各项调查与问询。
>
> https://www.wsj.com/articles/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-ceo-a6b49914

>
> [!quote]+
>
> 英伟达（Nvidia）董事会周一宣布，此前于11月12日辞职的黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）已重返公司，再次担任总裁兼首席执行官。
>
> 英伟达在声明中表示，该决定即刻生效。
>
> “在与黄仁勋先生进行了一系列讨论和会晤后，董事会一致投票决定让他复职。董事会对黄仁勋先生的坦诚以及他领导英伟达的能力感到满意。”
>
> 这一出人意料的举动推动英伟达股价飙升30%，并带动标普500指数开盘上涨近4%。
>
> 在此之前，美国总统唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）于周日晚间在社交媒体上写道：“我希望英伟达董事会能重新聘用黄仁勋。这对公司乃至整个美国来说，都是最好的结果。”
>
> 英伟达表示，决定让黄仁勋复职是参考了“来自美国政府高层的意见”。公司补充道：“基于这些意见，董事会确信黄仁勋先生的回归不会构成任何国家安全风险。”
>
> 黄仁勋在个人声明中表示，他“很荣幸能回到英伟达，在这一新工业革命的开端，领导这家全球最具影响力的科技公司之一。”
>
> 黄仁勋实际上一直担任着人工智能热潮的非官方“大使”，代表着那些支持人工智能发展的企业，以及该领域投入的数万亿美元资金。
>
> “我也衷心感谢我们的员工、股东、各行业领袖以及全球各地的合作伙伴，感谢他们给予的非凡支持，”黄仁勋补充道。
>
> 此次人事变动出现戏剧性反转。此前，英伟达新任董事长哈维·琼斯（Harvey Jones）曾于11月17日表示：“黄仁勋是自愿辞去总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务的。英伟达董事会一致接受了他的辞呈，且无意让他重返首席执行官职位。”
>
> 当天，英伟达临时首席执行官科莱特·克雷斯（Collette Kress）在接受采访时也曾表示，公司不会让黄仁勋复职。在《纽约时报》报道称黄（Huang）与一名被美国情报机构认定为中国间谍的女子关系密切后，他离开了英伟达（Nvidia）。随后，《金融时报》也跟进报道，称黄与该女子存在婚外情。
>
> 11月8日，黄在发给英伟达员工的一份备忘录中写道：“我对妻子不忠。我的行为伤害了她和我们的孩子。我所做的一切没有任何借口。我深感抱歉。”
>

> 黄仁勋在一份声明中表示：“我很荣幸能重返英伟达，在新一轮工业革命开启之际，领导这家全球最具影响力的科技公司之一。我怀着极其谦卑的心态承担起这一重任，并重申我的承诺。感谢英伟达董事会在整个过程中给予的信任与审慎考量。”

> 尽管要求黄仁勋回归的呼声日益高涨，但英伟达（Nvidia）董事长哈维·琼斯（Harvey Jones）上周曾表示，公司不会重新聘用他。
>
> 黄仁勋将英伟达从一家电子游戏芯片设计公司，打造成为人工智能处理器领域的主导供应商。他在公司芯片发展路线图、与主要客户的关系，以及与华盛顿方面的联络中，都发挥了核心作用。
>
> 11月12日，在被曝出婚外情（其中包括与一名被美国当局怀疑为中国从事间谍活动的商界女性有染——北京方面否认了这一指控）后，黄仁勋选择了辞职。
>
> 他的离职在从硅谷到台北，再到华盛顿的范围内引发了强烈反响。一份呼吁他复职的请愿书征集到了超过18万个签名，其中包括埃隆·马斯克（Elon Musk）的签名。这凸显了人们对这位在争议声中卸任的高管给予了异常强烈的支持。
>
> 董事会决定让黄仁勋回归，这不仅凸显了他在英伟达内部深远的影响力，也引发了人们的疑问：这家全球市值最高的公司之一，究竟在多大程度上依然依赖其联合创始人。
>
> 英伟达董事会周一表示，对黄仁勋的坦诚态度和领导能力感到满意；在听取了美国政府高级官员的意见后，董事会认为他的回归不会构成国家安全风险。
>
> 公司还表示，科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）将继续担任首席财务官。
>

> [IGN – 23 Nov 26](https://www.ign.com/articles/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-ceo-amid-donald-trump-social-media-pressure)
>

> ['I can’t wait to get back to work' — Nvidia Board Reinstates Jensen Huang as...](https://www.ign.com/articles/nvidia-board-reinstates-jensen-huang-as-ceo-amid-donald-trump-social-media-pressure)
>
> The Nvidia board has reinstated Jensen Huang as President, CEO and Board Director amid social media pressure from Donald Trump.
>
> [!quote]+
>
> 在唐纳德·特朗普（Donald Trump）通过社交媒体施压的背景下，英伟达（Nvidia）董事会已恢复黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）的总裁、首席执行官及董事会成员职务。
>
> 黄仁勋此前曾因涉及不忠行为及涉嫌从事间谍活动的丑闻而卸任英伟达首席执行官一职。如今，他重返公司；英伟达董事会表示，在与黄仁勋进行了一系列讨论和会晤后，董事会“一致投票决定恢复其职务”，并对黄仁勋的坦诚态度及其领导英伟达的能力感到满意。
>
> 英伟达进一步指出：“在做出这一决定的过程中，董事会听取了美国政府高层的意见。基于这些意见，董事会确信，黄仁勋的回归不会构成任何国家安全风险。”
>
> 上周，黄仁勋表示愿意重返他共同创立的公司，并就他给英伟达（Nvidia）及其家人所带来的问题表达了歉意。在当时发布的一份声明中，黄仁勋强调，如果英伟达董事会认为由他出任首席执行官（CEO）最符合公司利益，他愿意回归。一些英伟达员工及其他科技公司高管纷纷声援黄仁勋，呼吁让他重掌首席执行官一职。
>
> 英伟达董事会主席哈维·C·琼斯（Harvey C. Jones）发表了如下声明：
>
> “董事会认为，黄仁勋（Jensen）是领导英伟达（Nvidia）的合适人选；他重掌帅印，最符合我们股东、员工、合作伙伴及客户的利益。我们对黄仁勋充满信心，并期待在他重返公司领导岗位后与他携手共事。我们还要感谢科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress），她在担任英伟达首席财务官的同时，还出色地履行了临时首席执行官的职责。”
>
> 黄仁勋发表了一份个人声明：
>
> “我很荣幸能重返英伟达（Nvidia），在这一场全新工业革命的开端，执掌这家全球最具影响力的科技公司之一。我怀着极其谦卑的心态承担起这一重任，并重申我的坚定承诺。感谢英伟达董事会在整个过程中给予的信任与审慎考量。我特别感谢哈维·琼斯（Harvey Jones）在担任董事长期间所展现出的卓越领导力，也感谢科莱特·克雷斯（Colette Kress）及我们的高管团队在这一时期带领英伟达稳步前行。同时，我还要衷心感谢我们的员工、股东、各行业领袖以及全球合作伙伴所给予的鼎力支持。最重要的是，感谢我的家人给予我的爱与支持。我已经迫不及待想要投入工作了。”
>
> 英伟达（Nvidia）今日表示，已成立一个委员会，旨在调查有关黄仁勋（Jensen Huang）曾成为“外国情报行动”目标的报道，并强调调查工作将持续进行。英伟达称：“黄仁勋先生完全支持此次调查，并承诺将予以配合。”
>
> 与此同时，英伟达宣布成立“国家安全与出口管制委员会”，负责监督贸易合规事宜及评估国家安全风险。英伟达目前正在物色一位首席合规官，负责统筹全公司的合规工作，并直接向“提名与公司治理委员会”汇报。公司表示：“英伟达将继续配合政府正在进行的各项调查与问询。”
>
> 据报道，黄仁勋预计将于12月1日出席美国众议院外交事务委员会、情报委员会以及“美中战略竞争特设委员会”（简称“中国问题特设委员会”）的听证会。据美国消费者新闻与商业频道（CNBC）报道，众议员布莱恩·马斯特（Brian Mast，共和党，佛罗里达州）、约翰·穆勒纳尔（John Moolenaar，共和党，密歇根州）和里克·克劳福德（Rick Crawford，共和党，阿肯色州）——他们分别担任上述三个委员会的主席——在一份声明中表示：“美国民众需要得到答案，弄清黄仁勋先生及英伟达在‘允许危险的中国实体获取我们最先进芯片’一事中所扮演的角色，以及在此次事件中是否存在‘中国情报资产’（即受中国情报机构利用或控制的人员）参与其中。”
>

### [XNU Linux 允许 macOS 用户空间进程在 Linux 上运行](https://linux.do/t/topic/3229785)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-23 14:17 UTC · zh-CN · by 🐟

> [phoronix.com](https://www.phoronix.com/news/XNU-Linux)
>
> ![](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/6/a/8/6a82eeae1204f203d3a760d8238302991ab74e9e_2_690x431.webp)
>
> [XNU Linux Lets macOS Userspace Processes Run On Linux](https://www.phoronix.com/news/XNU-Linux)
>
> XNU Linux is a new opens-source project allowing macOS user-space software to run on Linux by loading the macOS kernel into it
>
> XNU Linux 是一个全新的开源项目，它通过将 macOS 内核加载到 Linux 系统中，使得 macOS 用户空间软件能够在 Linux 上运行。该项目基于苹果公司开源的 macOS XNU 内核组件构建，并经过适配，使其能够作为可加载的 Linux 内核模块运行。除了这个 XNU 内核模块外，整个系统基于未经修改的 ARM64 架构 Linux 系统。
>
> XNU Linux 使得 macOS 进程能够与 Linux 进程并排原生运行，且无需依赖任何虚拟机监视器（hypervisor）：
>
> “XNU Linux 项目利用苹果公司发布的源代码构建了 macOS 的开源内核——XNU，并将其作为可加载内核模块（xnu.ko）运行在未经修改的 ARM64 Linux 内核中。在 Linux 中运行的 XNU 内核可以直接驱动 CPU 和内存管理单元（MMU），因此 macOS 进程能够与 Linux 进程在同一 CPU 上原生并排运行，两者之间无需任何虚拟机监视器。通过一个小型接口模块（fki.ko），Linux 系统为 XNU 提供了内存、定时器、文件系统、网络及 GPU 资源支持。
>
> 在标准的 Ubuntu 内核环境下，通过 insmod xnu.ko 命令，即可引导由苹果官方安装程序创建的 macOS 27 系统磁盘，并进入桌面环境——包括 loginwindow、WindowServer、Dock、Finder、Safari 和 Chrome 等组件。”
>
> XNU Linux 依赖于苹果开源的 XNU 内核代码。至于 macOS 二进制文件，则需由用户自行从其现有的 macOS 安装环境或其他来源获取。
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/7/0/c/70cef6dabccd1cd84fc45973b5f5d8d629318de7_2_690x431.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/7/0/c/70cef6dabccd1cd84fc45973b5f5d8d629318de7.jpeg)
>
> 此 XNU Linux 仅适用于 ARM64 架构，而不支持 x86_64 架构。目前，所有的用户空间测试均是在 macOS 27 版本上进行的。
>
> [![image](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/optimized/4X/8/4/6/846c68565acf5fbdc826d80f3e7d894589b2a875_2_690x431.jpeg)](https://cdn3.ldstatic.com/original/4X/8/4/6/846c68565acf5fbdc826d80f3e7d894589b2a875.jpeg)
>
> Those curious about XNU Linux can learn more via the project’s [GitHub](https://github.com/AFK-surf/xnulinux).

### [交行万事达借记卡支持境外交易转人民币入账](https://linux.do/t/topic/3229780)

`linuxdo:前沿快讯` · T2 · 2026-11-23 14:16 UTC · zh-CN · by Gazes

> 交通银行万事达借记卡现已推出境外交易自动转人民币入账功能。该功能位于我的账户-万事达借记卡 更多功能-万事达借记卡境外交易转人民币管理。
>
> 启用此功能后，在境外消费时：
>
> 如美元账户（钞、汇）余额充足，依然扣除美元账户余额；
>
> 如美元账户余额不足，交易将以交易时交通银行售汇牌价转扣人民币账户，不占用便利化购汇额度；
>
> 如美元账户、人民币账户余额均不足，则交易无法完成。
>
> 启用此功能后，在境外退款时：
>
> 如原交易实际转为人民币扣款，或原交易不存在（如境外退税），退货时交易金额将按退货时交行美元结汇牌价转人民币入账，不占用便利化结汇额度；
>
> 如原交易存在，且实际扣款货币为美元，则退款将以美元入账美元（钞）账户。
>
> 请注意：该卡在境外的实际交易货币仍仅为美元。请注意多次货币转换可能导致汇率损失、结售汇牌价点差可能导致退款金额低于付款金额。
>
> 截至发稿时，交行万事达借记卡仍不支持境外预授权与3DS。
>
> 感谢 Song CR 投稿。
>
